response: {"findings":[{"issue":"IAM role policy grants overly broad permissions to all resources.","severity":"high","resource":"aws_iam_role_policy.order_worker_runtime","recommendation":"Restrict the policy to specific resources instead of using '*', e.g., specify the ARNs of the S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, and Secrets Manager secrets that the Lambda function needs access to."},{"issue":"Lambda function URL allows public access without authorization.","severity":"high","resource":"aws_lambda_function_url.checkout_callback","recommendation":"Change the authorization_type from 'NONE' to 'AWS_IAM' to restrict access to authenticated users."},{"issue":"Lambda function permission allows invocation from any principal.","severity":"high","resource":"aws_lambda_permission.storefront_invoke","recommendation":"Restrict the principal to specific AWS services or accounts that need to invoke the Lambda function instead of using '*', to limit exposure."},{"issue":"Sensitive environment variables are hardcoded in the Lambda function.","severity":"medium","resource":"aws_lambda_function.order_processor","recommendation":"Use AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store to manage sensitive information like STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and DB_PASSWORD instead of hardcoding them in the environment variables."},{"issue":"DynamoDB table point-in-time recovery is not enabled.","severity":"medium","resource":"aws_dynamodb_table.orders","recommendation":"Enable point-in-time recovery by setting 'enabled = true' in the point_in_time_recovery block to protect against accidental data loss."}]}
